items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bill and Steve and been with me through everything... We’ve been together 35 years, Bill Goodwin, Steve Gilmore and I.

ctx.x: Yeah, so I remember being in uh, when I was in L.A., uh a local the local, Donte’s, the local jazz

club wanted me, you know. They heard that I was in town so I gave them a pretty stiff price. I mean, I was used to five years in Europe, you know, I wasn’t going to work for scale. And I remember the club owner saying, “Stay here long enough, we’ll get you to for scale,” and I said, “I’m out of here,” you know. And by that point my marriage to Chan was kind of on the rocks, and I met Jill, and fell in love with Jill, my present wife, Jill Goodwin, who happens to be my, the sister of my drummer, Bill Goodwin.

items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: I joined Phil Woods’s band or we joined it was really like a cooperative band.

ctx.x: Did you get into it — I’ll just say “on purpose.” How did it occur?

Well it happened because I joined Phil Woods’s band or we joined it was really like a cooperative band. For some reason we played really well together in the original quartet. And Phil had his manager at that time who was also his record producer. And the guy was an accountant and he knew nothing about music. But he’d still tell you how to play. And I had been thinking about it, to say if that guy can do that I could do that gig and I could make ten times what I’m making on this record date, like he is. I was…

items.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999
items.q: Bill Goodwin, Steve Gilmore and I, we’ve been working together for 26 years now.

ctx.x: I found another quote that I liked from you. And it was I think in regard to the “Sun Suite” record, and after talking about the music said, “I am going to wait and see if it touched the public because that after all is the big kick.” So the public response to your work — I mean it almost goes without saying, but not in all cases with musicians.

I have a nice support group. I mean you’ve got to remember that — not remember, but like for instance Bill Goodwin, Steve Gilmore and I, we’ve been working together for 26 years now. Now we’re not household names, but we have a very nice audience around the world because we’ve garnered the audience the old fashioned way. We’ve gone around for 25 years playing in small joints for a hundred and two hundred people at a time. So we go back and we get maybe 250. I mean it’s not the megabucks that anybody’s interested…
